symbols.name: n
symbols.def: The number of observed process coordinates.

symbols.name: V
symbols.def: The observed coordinates repeated at every integer time.

symbols.name: L
symbols.def: The largest permitted absolute lag of a directed or shared-root relation.

symbols.name: H
symbols.def: The supplied exact summary, with directed edge set \(E_{\to}(H)\) and symmetric bidirected edge set \(E_{\leftrightarrow}(H)\).

symbols.name: X
symbols.def: The intervened coordinate.

symbols.name: Y
symbols.def: The outcome coordinate.

symbols.name: gamma
symbols.def: The treatment time is \(-\gamma\) and the outcome time is zero.

symbols.name: A
symbols.def: A fixed common input: each \(\mathcal A_i\) is one specified set, and every compatible model uses exactly this family; finiteness and nontriviality are imposed by \(\mathrm{ass:finite\text{-}alphabet}\).

symbols.name: ObsSpace
symbols.def: The single product sample space on which every compatible observational process law, cylinder event, and returned functional is defined.

symbols.name: x
symbols.def: The value imposed on \(X_{-\gamma}\).

symbols.name: y
symbols.def: The outcome event value at time zero.

symbols.name: R
symbols.space: Time-unrolled directed mixed graphs on \(V\times\mathbb Z\)
symbols.def: A translation-invariant time graph whose realized directed lags and bidirected offsets are bounded by \(L\), whose instantaneous directed slice is acyclic, and whose quotient summary is exactly \(H\).

symbols.name: Rclass
symbols.def: The exact bounded-lag refinement class defined in \(\mathrm{def:refinement\text{-}class}\).

symbols.name: Gmax
symbols.def: The time-unrolled graph containing every directed lag and bidirected offset permitted by \(H\) and \(L\).
symbols.role: saturated graph for the acyclic-summary reduction

symbols.name: M
symbols.def: A time-homogeneous causal model on a refinement \(R\), with observed variables taking values in the fixed family \(\mathcal A\) and pairwise shared exogenous roots for bidirected edges.

symbols.name: beta
symbols.def: The beta-mixing coefficient between the observed-process past and the future separated by \(k\) time steps.

symbols.name: Pobs
symbols.def: The entire observational law induced by \(M\) on the common path space \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\).

symbols.name: Mclass
symbols.def: The compatible-model class defined in \(\mathrm{def:model\text{-}class}\).

symbols.name: theta
symbols.def: The lag-specific micro total-effect event probability.

symbols.name: UID
symbols.def: The refinement-uniform micro-effect identification predicate defined in \(\mathrm{def:uniform\text{-}identification}\).

symbols.name: Cylinder
symbols.def: Here \(S\subset V\times\mathbb Z\) is finite and \(a\in\prod_{(i,t)\in S}\mathcal A_i\); thus every cylinder is a subset of the fixed common path space.

symbols.name: pCyl
symbols.def: The probability under \(P_M\) of a finite cylinder in \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\).

symbols.name: Lang
symbols.def: Finite expressions formed from cylinder probabilities by rational constants, finite sums, finite products, and ratios with positive denominators.

symbols.name: F
symbols.def: A finite arithmetic expression in \(\mathcal L_{\mathrm{cyl}}(\mathcal A)\) returned by the identification procedure and evaluated only on laws over the fixed path space.

symbols.name: CF
symbols.def: The finite collection of observed cylinders whose probabilities occur in \(F\).

symbols.name: dF
symbols.def: The number of cylinder coordinates required by \(F\).

symbols.name: RoleState
symbols.def: A state records a bounded frontier of temporal roles, random versus fixed status, bidirected connectivity through the eliminated past, directed reachability, admissible offset sets, admissible instantaneous orders, and the typed kernel identity accumulated along the path.

symbols.name: FDCert
symbols.def: A finite lag-template consisting of a radius, a nonempty mediator-role set, and an observed blocking-role set, subject to the uniform graphical conditions in \(\mathrm{def:micro\text{-}frontdoor\text{-}family}\).

symbols.name: FDfamily
symbols.def: The explicit uniform micro-SCG front-door family constructed in \(\mathrm{def:micro\text{-}frontdoor\text{-}family}\).

symbols.name: cA
symbols.def: The certificate induced by the graphical sets in Theorem 1 of Assaad (2025), with membership asserted in \(\mathrm{thm:frontdoor\text{-}frontier}\).

symbols.name: Fc
symbols.def: For each front-door certificate, the generalized front-door arithmetic functional compiled by the frontier theorem.

symbols.name: Hfdout
symbols.def: The two-coordinate, binary, lag-one input constructed in \(\mathrm{def:frontdoor\text{-}outside\text{-}witness}\).

symbols.name: Fout
symbols.def: The finite-cylinder functional compiled by the complete witness trace.

symbols.name: Traceout
symbols.def: The five-state offset-sensitive trace constructed in \(\mathrm{def:frontdoor\text{-}outside\text{-}trace}\).

symbols.name: Bstar
symbols.def: The temporal radius and certificate-size bound derived by \(\mathrm{oeq:uniform\text{-}normal\text{-}form}\).

symbols.name: LagHedge
symbols.def: A finite pair of temporal-role graphs, rational structural tables on the fixed alphabets \(\mathcal A\), and a common positive role law that lifts to two exact-summary stationary models on \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\) with unequal target values.

symbols.name: TID
symbols.def: The procedure constructed from the handle in \(\mathrm{def:transducer\text{-}handle}\).

symbols.name: Mzero
symbols.def: The first model encoded by a lag-switch-hedge certificate.

symbols.name: Mone
symbols.def: The second model encoded by a lag-switch-hedge certificate.

symbols.name: T
symbols.def: The number of consecutive observed time points used for estimation.

symbols.name: Cbeta
symbols.def: The multiplicative constant in the geometric absolute-regularity bound.

symbols.name: rho
symbols.def: The geometric absolute-regularity ratio.

symbols.name: alpha
symbols.def: The nominal two-sided Wald error probability.

symbols.name: zcrit
symbols.def: The two-sided Gaussian critical value at level \(\alpha\).

symbols.name: Z
symbols.sig: \(Z_t=(\mathbf 1\{C_{\mathcal A,j}\text{ occurs at shift }t\}:1\le j\le d_F)\)
symbols.def: The indicator vector for every cylinder probability appearing in the returned expression \(F\).

symbols.name: pF
symbols.def: The vector of population cylinder probabilities required by \(F\).

symbols.name: phat
symbols.def: The overlapping-cylinder frequency vector, with boundary terms omitted in the finite usual way.

symbols.name: Omega
symbols.def: The long-run covariance of the cylinder-indicator process.

symbols.name: K
symbols.def: The fixed Bartlett kernel \(K(u)=(1-|u|)\mathbf 1\{|u|\le1\}\), used at a scaled lag to form the modified Bartlett weights of Newey and West (1987).

symbols.name: hT
symbols.def: The largest empirical autocovariance lag entering the HAC estimator.

symbols.name: Gammahat
symbols.def: The centered empirical lag-\(k\) covariance of the cylinder-indicator vector.

symbols.name: Omegahat
symbols.def: The Newey--West modified-Bartlett estimator based on centered cylinder indicators, with weight \(1-k/(h_T+1)\) at lag \(k\le h_T\).

symbols.name: gradF
symbols.def: The ordinary gradient of the returned rational cylinder functional on its positive domain.

symbols.name: thetahat
symbols.def: The returned functional evaluated at overlapping cylinder frequencies.

symbols.name: vF
symbols.def: The delta-method long-run variance.

symbols.name: vhat
symbols.sig: \(\widehat v_F=\nabla F(\widehat p_F)^{\mathsf T}\widehat\Omega_F\nabla F(\widehat p_F)\)
symbols.def: The HAC delta-method variance estimate.

assumptions.condition: \(P_M(C_{\mathcal A}(S,a))>0\quad\forall S\subset V\times\mathbb Z\text{ finite},\ \forall a\in\prod_{(i,t)\in S}\mathcal A_i\).

standard.name: modified Bartlett lag window in equation (5)

definitions.name: Positive stationary bounded-lag semi-Markovian class
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)=\{M=(R,\mathcal A,f,U):R\in\mathfrak R(H,L),\text{ the observed state-space family is exactly the fixed input }\mathcal A,\ M\text{ satisfies }\mathrm{ass:finite\text{-}alphabet},\mathrm{ass:semi\text{-}markovian},\mathrm{ass:time\text{-}homogeneous},\mathrm{ass:strict\text{-}stationarity},\mathrm{ass:cylinder\text{-}positivity}\}\).

definitions.name: Uniform micro-effect identification
definitions.construction: \(\operatorname{UID}(H,L,\mathcal A,X,Y,\gamma,x,y)=1\iff[ P_{M_0}=P_{M_1}\text{ as measures on }\Omega_{\mathcal A}\Rightarrow\theta_{M_0}(y;x)=\theta_{M_1}(y;x)]\ \forall M_0,M_1\in\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)\).

definitions.name: Finite-cylinder arithmetic language
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal L_{\mathrm{cyl}}(\mathcal A)=\operatorname{closure}_{+,-,\times,/}\{P_M(C_{\mathcal A}(S,a)):S\subset V\times\mathbb Z\text{ finite},\ a\in\prod_{(i,t)\in S}\mathcal A_i\}\), where every \(P_M\) is a law on \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\) and division is defined only at positive denominators.

definitions.name: Lag-robust intrinsic-district handle
definitions.construction: Adapt the possible-c-component region recursion of Jaber--Ribeiro--Zhang--Bareinboim and the intrinsic-set fixing operator of Richardson--Robins--Evans--Shpitser to \(\mathsf S(H,L,\mathcal A,X,Y,\gamma)\); augment each state by temporal-role offsets, instantaneous-order constraints, boundary bidirected connectivity, and a typed kernel identity over cylinders in \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\), and use periodic hedge cutting as the finite-state pumping handle.

definitions.name: Uniform micro-SCG front-door criterion family
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak F_{\mathrm{FD}}(H,L,\mathcal A,X,Y,\gamma)=\{c=(b,\mathcal D,\mathcal B):b\in\mathbb N_0,\ \varnothing\ne\mathcal D\subseteq(V\setminus\{X,Y\})\times[-b,0],\ \mathcal B\subseteq(V\setminus\{Y\})\times[-b,0],\text{ and for every }R\in\mathfrak R(H,L),\text{ (i) }\mathcal D\text{ meets every proper directed path from }X_{-\gamma}\text{ to }Y_0,\text{ (ii) }\mathcal B\text{ m-separates }X_{-\gamma}\text{ from }\mathcal D\text{ after deleting arrows out of }X_{-\gamma},\text{ (iii) }\mathcal B\cup\{X_{-\gamma}\}\text{ m-separates }\mathcal D\text{ from }Y_0\text{ after deleting arrows out of }\mathcal D,\text{ and (iv) no role in }\mathcal B\text{ is a descendant of }X_{-\gamma}\}\). The same finite role templates \(\mathcal D,\mathcal B\) are used in every refinement, so their generalized front-door sums are expressions in \(\mathcal L_{\mathrm{cyl}}(\mathcal A)\).

definitions.name: Back-door-identified input outside the front-door family
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{out}}=(H_{\mathrm{out}},1,\mathcal A^{\mathrm{bin}},1,2,1,0,1)\), where \(V=\{1,2\}\), \(\mathcal A^{\mathrm{bin}}_1=\mathcal A^{\mathrm{bin}}_2=\{0,1\}\), and \(H_{\mathrm{out}}\) has the single directed edge \(1\to2\), no directed self-loop, and no bidirected edge. Thus \(X=1\), \(Y=2\), \(L=\gamma=1\), \(x=0\), and \(y=1\).

definitions.name: Complete TID-SCG trace for the outside-class witness
definitions.construction: For \(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{out}}\), the complete trace is \(s_0\to s_1\to s_2\to s_3\to s_4\): \(s_0\) initializes the query frontier \(\{X_{-1},Y_0\}\); \(s_1\) closes it in the maximal legal refinement to \(\{X_{-1},X_0,Y_0\}\) and records the nonempty admissible edge-offset set \(\Delta_{12}\subseteq\{0,1\}\); \(s_2\) records that every admissible branch has singleton intrinsic districts because \(H_{\mathrm{out}}\) has no bidirected edge, with the order constraint \(X_0\prec Y_0\) when \(0\in\Delta_{12}\); \(s_3\) fixes the two treatment-coordinate roles and compiles the branch-independent kernels \(q_Y(1\mid0,a)=P(Y_0=1\mid X_{-1}=0,X_0=a)\) and \(q_0(a)=P(X_0=a)\); \(s_4\) sums the natural instantaneous treatment role and returns \(\operatorname{SUCCESS}(F_{\mathrm{out}})\), where \(F_{\mathrm{out}}(P)=\sum_{a\in\mathcal A_1}q_Y(1\mid0,a)q_0(a)\). Positivity makes every conditional cylinder well defined, and the recorded offset set covers lag zero, lag one, and their simultaneous presence without refinement enumeration.

definitions.name: Positive stationary lag-switch regression pair
definitions.construction: For the fixed binary input \(V=\{1,2,3\}\), \(\mathcal A_i=\{0,1\}\) for every \(i\in V\), \(X=1\), \(Y=3\), \(L=\gamma=1\), \(q=1/5\), and \(r=1/10\), set in model zero \(O_{1,t}=(R_t\wedge O_{2,t-1})\oplus U_t\), \(O_{2,t}=O_{1,t}\oplus N_t\), and \(O_{3,t}=O_{2,t-1}\oplus E_t\); set in model one \(O_{2,t}=(R'_t\wedge O_{1,t-1})\oplus U'_t\), \(O_{1,t}=O_{2,t}\oplus N'_t\), and \(O_{3,t}=O_{2,t-1}\oplus E'_t\), with \(R_t,U_t,R'_t,U'_t\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\), \(N_t,N'_t\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(q)\), and \(E_t,E'_t\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(r)\), mutually independent across named sequences and time. Both models use exactly this same \(\mathcal A\) and hence induce laws on the same \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\).

definitions.name: Cylinder modified-Bartlett HAC delta-method variance
definitions.construction: \(\widehat\Omega_F=\widehat\Gamma_0+\sum_{k=1}^{h_T}K(k/(h_T+1))(\widehat\Gamma_k+\widehat\Gamma_k^{\mathsf T})\) and \(\widehat v_F=\nabla F(\widehat p_F)^{\mathsf T}\widehat\Omega_F\nabla F(\widehat p_F)\), where \(K(k/(h_T+1))=1-k/(h_T+1)\) for \(1\le k\le h_T\).

statements.statement: Fix \(\mathcal A\). Let two finite temporal-role semi-Markovian SCMs have observed role values in this same family, legal lags bounded by \(L\), a common strictly positive rational observed role law, unequal distributions of the designated outcome role under intervention on the designated treatment role, and an acyclic union of lag-zero coordinate relations. The independent-shift product construction yields \(M_0,M_1\in\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)\) with \(P_{M_0}=P_{M_1}\) as measures on \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\) and \(\theta_{M_0}(y;x)\ne\theta_{M_1}(y;x)\); independent auxiliary edge channels valued in the fixed alphabets make both summaries exactly \(H\) without changing the separation.
statements.justification: This lemma turns a bounded graphical collision into the whole-process stationary countermodels required for semantic nonidentification.
statements.gap: Shpitser--Pearl construct finite fixed-ADMG hedge models, while Jahn--Karnik--Schulman localize fixed-graph hedges; neither result preserves strict stationarity, time homogeneity, exact summaries, and equality of the entire process law under a refinement switch.
statements.consumer: Every rejecting state of \(\operatorname{TID\text{-}SCG}(H,L,\mathcal A,X,Y,\gamma,x,y)\) obtains an auditable finite countermodel on the fixed product alphabet rather than an inconclusive failure code.

statements.statement: Fix \(\mathcal A\). If the directed part of \(H\) is acyclic and has no directed self-loop, let \(G^\star\) contain every permitted directed lag and bidirected offset. The ancestors of \(\{X_{-\gamma},Y_0\}\) in \(G^\star\) lie in \(V\times[-\gamma-(n-1)L,0]\), contain at most \(n(nL+1)\) vertices, and one ordinary ID call on this ancestral ADMG is sound and complete for uniform identification over \(\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)\), with every returned probability evaluated on the common product alphabet.
statements.justification: The proposition supplies a nontrivial solved subclass and a required reduction test for the general transducer.
statements.gap: Assaad, Devijver, Gaussier, Gössler, and Meynaoui use a densest candidate full-time graph to validate adjustment under causal sufficiency, and Jahn--Karnik--Schulman analyze one fully specified periodic latent-confounded graph. This reduction instead uses one saturated ancestral ADMG to decide general fixing-based identification uniformly over unknown lag refinements and supplies exact-summary stationary negative witnesses.
statements.consumer: Acyclic EasyRCA summaries can be screened immediately with an ordinary finite ID implementation.

statements.statement: For the fixed binary family in \(\mathrm{def:lag\text{-}switch\text{-}regression}\), the two models belong to the same \(\mathfrak M(H,1,\mathcal A)\), have exact common summary \(1\to2\), \(2\to1\), \(2\to3\), no bidirected edges, the same strictly positive entire stationary observed law as measures on \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\), and separately identifiable refinement-specific effects, but \(P_{M_0}(O_{3,0}=1\mid\operatorname{do}(O_{1,-1}=0))=13/50\) and \(P_{M_1}(O_{3,0}=1\mid\operatorname{do}(O_{1,-1}=0))=1/2\).
statements.justification: This positive collision proves that per-refinement ID and formula enumeration are not complete for the uniform query.
statements.gap: The abstraction hierarchy separates graphwise identification from common identification abstractly; this proposition gives a strictly stationary finite-alphabet micro-effect collision with exact arithmetic and whole-law equality.
statements.consumer: The example is a mandatory rejection regression test for any implementation and prevents false causal rankings in EasyRCA.

statements.statement: For the fixed common alphabet input \(\mathcal A\), use \(\mathrm{def:transducer\text{-}handle}\) to construct a bounded uniform fixing normal form and derive an explicit computable \(B_\star(n,L,\gamma)\) such that every reachable state either compiles one expression \(F\in\mathcal L_{\mathrm{cyl}}(\mathcal A)\) from cylinders in \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\), valid for all compatible refinements, or extracts within radius and encoding size \(B_\star(n,L,\gamma)\) a finite lag-switch-hedge role pair on those same alphabets satisfying the premises of \(\mathrm{lem:stationary\text{-}lift}\), including states where every refinement is individually identifiable but the refinement-specific functionals disagree.
statements.justification: This is the theorem-level open kernel: it must establish both bounded common-functional compilation and bounded positive stationary obstruction extraction.
statements.gap: Fixed-ADMG ID, PAG regions, and periodic hedge cutting each preserve only one of fixed vertices, fixed lags, or a single graph; none gives a state invariant for lag-offset uncertainty and common-law functional disagreement.
statements.consumer: The normal form makes a definitive identification or abstention decision possible from a latent-confounded summary graph without refinement enumeration or unrestricted elimination.

statements.statement: For every feasible \((H,L,\mathcal A,X,Y,\gamma,x,y)\), \(\operatorname{TID\text{-}SCG}(H,L,\mathcal A,X,Y,\gamma,x,y)\) terminates after at most \(B_\star(n,L,\gamma)\) state transitions and exactly one outcome holds: \(\operatorname{SUCCESS}(F)\) with \(F(P_M)=\theta_M(y;x)\) for every \(M\in\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)\), where \(F\in\mathcal L_{\mathrm{cyl}}(\mathcal A)\) is evaluated on cylinders of \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\), or \(\operatorname{FAIL}(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{lag}}(\mathcal A))\) encoding \(M_0,M_1\in\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)\) with \(P_{M_0}=P_{M_1}\) as measures on \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\) and \(\theta_{M_0}(y;x)\ne\theta_{M_1}(y;x)\). Moreover, \(\operatorname{TID\text{-}SCG}(H,L,\mathcal A,X,Y,\gamma,x,y)=\operatorname{SUCCESS}(F)\iff\operatorname{UID}(H,L,\mathcal A,X,Y,\gamma,x,y)=1\).
statements.justification: The dichotomy is the first sound-and-complete graph-native decision theorem for lag-specific micro effects under latent-confounded summary uncertainty.
statements.gap: Assaad, Devijver, Gaussier, Gössler, and Meynaoui give causally sufficient SCG total-effect adjustment conditions; Ferreira--Assaad give completeness for linear direct effects under causal sufficiency; Assaad gives latent-confounded front-door sufficiency; and Ferreira--Assaad separately give macro do-calculus completeness. None covers a nonparametric lag-specific micro total effect under hidden confounding. Jahn--Karnik--Schulman decide one fully specified periodic graph, Jaber and coauthors decide a PAG class on a fixed finite vertex set, and Shpitser--Pearl decide one fixed ADMG rather than an exact-summary stationary refinement class.
statements.consumer: EasyRCA can attach a causal transmission score only to successful lag queries and can display a concrete certificate when it must abstain.

statements.statement: For every fixed finite alphabet family \(\mathcal A\), the graphical criterion in Theorem 1 of Assaad (2025) induces an explicit certificate \(c_{\mathrm A}\in\mathfrak F_{\mathrm{FD}}(H,L,\mathcal A,X,Y,\gamma)\). For every \(c\in\mathfrak F_{\mathrm{FD}}(H,L,\mathcal A,X,Y,\gamma)\), \(\operatorname{TID\text{-}SCG}(H,L,\mathcal A,X,Y,\gamma,x,y)\) follows the corresponding fixing sequence, returns \(\operatorname{SUCCESS}(F_c)\), and \(F_c\in\mathcal L_{\mathrm{cyl}}(\mathcal A)\) is the generalized front-door functional certified by \(c\); for \(c=c_{\mathrm A}\), this is algebraically Assaad's published functional. For the concrete input \(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{out}}\), \(\mathfrak F_{\mathrm{FD}}(H_{\mathrm{out}},1,\mathcal A^{\mathrm{bin}},1,2,1)=\varnothing\) because there is no non-treatment, non-outcome mediator coordinate, while the complete trace \(\mathfrak t_{\mathrm{out}}\) returns \(\operatorname{SUCCESS}(F_{\mathrm{out}})\) and \(F_{\mathrm{out}}(P_M)=P_M(Y_0=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_{-1}=0))\) for every \(M\in\mathfrak M(H_{\mathrm{out}},1,\mathcal A^{\mathrm{bin}})\). Hence the successful TID-SCG region strictly contains this generic front-door family, with Assaad's criterion as a proved member.
statements.justification: The frontier theorem proves universal inclusion for an explicit family of front-door criteria, embeds the published criterion, and supplies a fully traced identified input outside the family.
statements.gap: Assaad's theorem is one sufficient front-door criterion. The present result proves it is an instance of a larger explicit uniform front-door family, maps every member of that family to a successful transducer certificate, and then verifies strict containment using a lag-one back-door-identified query with no eligible mediator coordinate.
statements.consumer: EasyRCA can retain every published or generalized SCG front-door identification while certifying additional lag effects, and the five-state trace supplies an executable regression test for that strict gain.

statements.statement: Fix \(\mathcal A\) and condition on \(\operatorname{TID\text{-}SCG}(H,L,\mathcal A,X,Y,\gamma,x,y)=\operatorname{SUCCESS}(F)\). For one stationary trajectory in \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\), geometric beta mixing and boundedness of the indicators of the finitely many returned cylinders \(C_{\mathcal A,j}\) imply the moment and mixing hypotheses used for Newey--West HAC consistency. With modified Bartlett weights \(1-k/(h_T+1)\), \(h_T\to\infty\), and \(h_T=o(T^{1/4})\), \(\widehat\Omega_F\overset p\to\Omega_F\), \(\sqrt T(\widehat\theta_F-\theta_M(y;x))\Rightarrow N(0,v_F)\), \(\widehat v_F\overset p\to v_F\), and \(P_M\{\theta_M(y;x)\in[\widehat\theta_F\pm z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\widehat v_F/T}]\}\to1-\alpha\). The limit is invariant under algebraically equivalent expressions in \(\mathcal L_{\mathrm{cyl}}(\mathcal A)\) after redundant simplex coordinates are removed.
statements.justification: A graphically identified cylinder functional becomes operational only with dependence-aware single-trajectory uncertainty quantification.
statements.gap: Bhattacharya--Nabi--Shpitser develop hidden-graph influence-function estimators for independent samples, while Viviano--Bradic treat different time-series causal targets; neither gives a generic HAC delta method for overlapping cylinders emitted by a graph algorithm.
statements.consumer: EasyRCA obtains confidence intervals for identified lag-specific transmission probabilities from one stationary regime.

statements.statement: For the fixed \(\mathcal A\), when \(L=0\), the refinement class contains one finite static ADMG on \(V\), \(\operatorname{TID\text{-}SCG}(H,0,\mathcal A,X,Y,0,x,y)\) reduces to ordinary ID on the common product alphabet, \(F\) equals the ordinary ID functional on success, and \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{lag}}(\mathcal A)\) reduces to an ordinary query-specific hedge on failure.
statements.justification: The static boundary is the required sanity reduction to the complete fixed-ADMG benchmark.
statements.gap: This is a reduction check rather than a novelty claim.
statements.consumer: Users recover standard ID behavior without a separate implementation when no temporal uncertainty is present.

statements.statement: For any finite collection of EasyRCA lag-specific transmission queries defined on one fixed coordinate set and alphabet family \(\mathcal A\), rank only pairs for which \(\operatorname{TID\text{-}SCG}(H,L,\mathcal A,X,Y,\gamma,x,y)=\operatorname{SUCCESS}(F)\); if their population scores are separated by a fixed positive margin, the plug-in ranking is consistent, while every failed query is accompanied by its \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{lag}}(\mathcal A)\) certificate and is excluded rather than assigned a causal score.
statements.justification: The proposition states the precise consumer contract: identified comparisons are ranked and unresolved comparisons trigger certified abstention.
statements.gap: EasyRCA assumes jointly independent noises and compares adjustment-based direct effects; it does not propagate latent-confounding identification failures into its ranking.
statements.consumer: Operators receive a causal ranking only where the summary abstraction supports one, with explicit reasons for missing edges.

sampling_model.design: One consecutive trajectory in the fixed common path space \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\) from a stationary regime \(M\in\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)\); identification is population-level and sampling uncertainty comes from temporal dependence.
sampling_model.units: Overlapping finite cylinders \(C_{\mathcal A}(S,a)\) on the fixed product alphabet, indexed by their terminal time.
sampling_model.treatment: A hypothetical intervention \(\operatorname{do}(X_{-\gamma}=x)\); no experimental assignments are observed.
sampling_model.overlap: Every cylinder assignment in the fixed product alphabet has positive probability, hence every denominator cylinder used by the returned expression is positive.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Probabilities of the returned \(\mathcal A\)-cylinders are estimated by empirical frequencies and their long-run covariance by the modified-Bartlett Newey--West estimator with \(h_T\to\infty\) and \(h_T=o(T^{1/4})\).

Transactions on Machine Learning Research. arXiv:2406.05805. Primary-source locator: Lemmas 4.1--4.5, Theorem 1 and its proof, and the concluding completeness discussion.

Shpitser, Ilya, and Judea Pearl (2008). Complete identification methods for the causal hierarchy. Journal of Machine Learning Research 9, 1941--1979. Primary-source locator: the recursive ID algorithm and hedge completeness results in Sections 3--4, with countermodel constructions in Appendix A.

Jahn, Erik L., Karthik Karnik, and Leonard J. Schulman (2025). Causal identification in time series models. Proceedings of the Fourth Conference on Causal Learning and Reasoning, PMLR 275, 1435--1449. arXiv:2504.20172. Primary-source locator: Theorem 1.1, Algorithm 2, and Section 4.1.

Jaber, Amin, Adèle H. Ribeiro, Jiji Zhang, and Elias Bareinboim (2022). Causal identification under Markov equivalence: calculus, algorithm, and completeness. Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 35. Primary-source locator: abstract and the soundness-and-completeness results for conditional-effect identification from a PAG.

Richardson, Thomas S., James M. Robins, Robin J. Evans, and Ilya Shpitser (2023). Nested Markov properties for acyclic directed mixed graphs. Annals of Statistics 51, 334--361. Primary-source locator: the fixing operation, reachable graphs, and intrinsic sets in Sections 2--4.

Ferreira, Simon, and Charles K. Assaad (2025). Identifying macro conditional independencies and macro total effects in summary causal graphs with latent confounding. Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence 39(25), 26787--26795. doi:10.1609/aaai.v39i25.34882. Primary-source locator: abstract and the macro-query definitions and do-calculus completeness result.

Ferreira, Simon, and Charles K. Assaad (2024). Identifiability of direct effects from summary causal graphs. Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence 38(18), 20387--20394. doi:10.1609/aaai.v38i18.30021. Primary-source locator: abstract and introduction, p. 1, https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/download/30021/31795.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 gives sufficient summary-graph front-door conditions and a common do-free expression for selected micro total effects under latent confounding.
The ID algorithm returns an observational functional or a hedge and is complete for a fixed finite ADMG.

Under causal sufficiency, the PMLR abstract describes necessary-and-sufficient graphical conditions for SCG total-effect identification and the paper supplies adjustment sets; the proceedings PDF states Theorem 2 as a sufficient-condition result.

tldr: SCG identification is already developed in several neighboring lanes: the PMLR abstract of Assaad, Devijver, Gaussier, Gössler, and Meynaoui reports necessary-and-sufficient causally sufficient total-effect adjustment conditions, Ferreira and Assaad give complete linear direct-effect identification under causal sufficiency, Assaad gives a latent-confounded front-door sufficient result for selected micro total effects, and Ferreira and Assaad give do-calculus completeness for macro interventions under latent confounding. None of these results decides a nonparametric lag-specific micro total-effect distribution uniformly over positive semi-Markovian refinements with hidden confounding. Fix one finite alphabet family \(\mathcal A\) as a common input, so every compatible SCM induces its entire observed law on the same path space \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\). Because an SCG hides lags and instantaneous orderings that determine latent-projection districts, identification in each compatible refinement need not produce one causal functional of that common observed process law. The focal object is \(\operatorname{TID\text{-}SCG}(H,L,\mathcal A,X,Y,\gamma,x,y)\), a finite offset-sensitive intrinsic-district transducer that returns either one arithmetic functional of finitely many \(\mathcal A\)-cylinders for \(P_M(Y_0=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X_{-\gamma}=x))\) over every \(M\in\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)\) or a bounded lag-switch hedge encoding two models in that same class with equal laws on \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\) and unequal effects. The project derives an explicit termination radius, embeds Assaad's criterion in an explicit generic micro-SCG front-door family, maps every member of that family to a successful certificate, and gives a complete five-state trace for a lag-one identified query outside the family. It also reduces to ordinary ID on the static boundary and adds modified-Bartlett Newey--West delta-method inference for any returned functional. The bounded uniform fixing normal form remains the first-class open question; independent-shift lifting, an acyclic-summary reduction, and a positive stationary lag-switch collision are the supporting proof obligations and destructive tests.

project_justification.gap: The PMLR abstract of Assaad, Devijver, Gaussier, Gössler, and Meynaoui reports necessary-and-sufficient singleton total-effect conditions for SCGs under causal sufficiency and the paper provides adjustment sets; Ferreira--Assaad completely characterize linear direct effects under the same no-hidden-confounding boundary. Assaad's hidden-confounded micro-total-effect theorem supplies one front-door sufficient formula but no generic front-door-class frontier or complete micro-effect decision rule, while Ferreira--Assaad prove completeness only for macro interventions on whole SCG clusters. Jahn--Karnik--Schulman bound ID after the periodic fine graph is known, Jaber and coauthors prove completeness for a fixed finite PAG, and Shpitser--Pearl give functional-or-hedge completeness for one fixed ADMG. None decides, for a fixed common finite alphabet family \(\mathcal A\), whether one nonparametric lag-specific micro total-effect functional is valid over every model in \(\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)\) or returns two such models with equal entire laws on \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\) when refinement-specific functionals disagree.
project_justification.niche: Causally sufficient SCG total effects can be handled by adjustment, linear direct effects admit a separate complete characterization, and a defined family of latent-confounded front-door templates covers mediated configurations including Assaad's criterion. Macro do-calculus acts on entire temporal clusters and therefore does not answer an intervention on one coordinate at one lag. The remaining latent-confounded micro query requires district fixing across unknown temporal roles while holding the observed coordinate alphabets and product sample space fixed. Bounded lag and time homogeneity make these roles finitely describable, but quotienting time can destroy fixability, a PAG keeps a fixed finite vertex set, and a known-periodic-graph bound presupposes the fine graph. This leaves a distinct common-functional problem under simultaneous lag, ordering, and hidden-confounding uncertainty on one common observed-law domain.
project_justification.fill: The lag-robust intrinsic-district transducer takes \(H,L,\mathcal A,X,Y,\gamma,x,y\) and targets a nonparametric semi-Markovian lag-specific micro total-effect distribution rather than an adjustment estimand, a linear direct-effect coefficient, or a macro cluster effect. Its state carries offsets, fixing status, boundary districts, admissible instantaneous orders, and typed identities over cylinders of \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\). An explicit generic front-door family is mapped member-by-member into successful transducer traces, contains Assaad's criterion as a proved instance, and is strictly contained by a concrete lag-one back-door success with a complete five-state trace. The normal-form theorem compiles one common finite-cylinder functional or extracts a finite temporal-role collision; independent shifts and exact-summary padding then convert the collision into positive stationary countermodels in \(\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)\) with equal entire observed laws on that same product space.

related_work: Assaad, Devijver, Gaussier, Gössler, and Meynaoui (2024), Assumption 1 on p. 175, impose causal sufficiency and study the singleton total effect \(P(y_t\mid\operatorname{do}(x_{t-\gamma}))\). Their PMLR abstract describes necessary-and-sufficient SCG conditions and their paper supplies adjustment sets; Theorem 2 on pp. 184--185 is worded as a sufficient-condition theorem. In either formulation, the result is an adjustment theorem with no hidden common causes, not a fixing result for semi-Markovian latent confounding and not a certificate for disagreement across refinement-specific functionals. Ferreira and Assaad (2024), abstract and introduction on p. 1, give a complete characterization and two finite adjustment sets for linear direct effects under no hidden confounding. Their target is a linear direct-effect coefficient, not the present nonparametric lag-specific micro total-effect distribution. Yvernes, Devijver, and Gaussier (2025) give necessary-and-sufficient common-adjustment conditions under causal sufficiency; that output is an adjustment set rather than a general hidden-variable identifying functional. Assaad (2025), Lemmas 4.1--4.5 and Theorem 1, establishes a common front-door functional for selected micro total effects under latent confounding and sufficient SCG conditions. The explicit family \(\mathfrak F_{\mathrm{FD}}\) retains the front-door architecture through uniform path interception and two uniform back-door separations, contains Assaad's criterion as a proved certificate, and \(\mathrm{thm:frontdoor\text{-}frontier}\) proves that every member maps to TID-SCG success before giving a fully traced success outside the family. Ferreira and Assaad (2025), abstract and macro-query definitions, prove do-calculus soundness and completeness for interventions on whole SCG clusters under latent confounding. A macro intervention sets an entire time-series cluster and does not identify the effect of setting only \(X_{-\gamma}\). Jahn, Karnik, and Schulman (2025), Theorem 1.1, Algorithm 2, and Section 4.1, bound the segment needed to apply ordinary ID to one fully specified periodic latent-confounded graph; the unknown refinement class and cross-refinement functional agreement are outside that input and output. Jaber, Ribeiro, Zhang, and Bareinboim (2022) prove sound-and-complete conditional-effect identification for the Markov-equivalence class represented by one finite PAG. Their vertices are fixed and their output does not encode translation-invariant lag roles or strict-stationarity witnesses. Shpitser and Pearl (2008), Sections 3--4 and Appendix A, give the functional-or-hedge completeness theorem for one fixed finite ADMG; their hedges do not by themselves preserve time homogeneity, exact SCG summaries, and equality of an entire stationary process law. Richardson, Robins, Evans, and Shpitser (2023), Sections 2--4, provide fixing kernels, reachable graphs, and intrinsic sets for a fixed ADMG; these objects inform the state language but their invariance must be re-established under offset uncertainty. Yvernes and coauthors' abstraction hierarchy clarifies why graphwise success, a common proof, and common-functional identification differ. Bhattacharya, Nabi, and Shpitser (2022) inform compilation of fixed-graph functionals into estimators under independent sampling. Viviano and Bradic (2023) provide a beta-mixing inference lane for a different time-series target. Newey and West (1987), equation (5) and Theorems 1--2 on pp. 704--706, give the modified Bartlett weights, positive-semidefiniteness, and consistency under \(h_T\to\infty\) with \(h_T/T^{1/4}\to0\). Duarte and coauthors (2024) reduce discrete causal bounds to polynomial programs, but unrestricted polynomial elimination is excluded from the graph-native kernel. EasyRCA supplies the consumer and currently ranks adjustment-based direct effects under independent noises. All comparisons in the present uniform-identification claim hold \(\mathcal A\) fixed: model pairs are compared as laws on one \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\), and every returned cylinder functional has that same domain.
technical_internal_limitation: Strict stationarity and structural lag \(L\) do not imply a finite-order Markov observed law on \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\); a lag-one shared-root process can have cylinder predictions that depend on arbitrarily long histories. The transducer may therefore use a bounded graph frontier and identities among \(\mathcal A\)-cylinders, but its proof cannot factor the observed process as an order-\(L\) transition kernel. Likewise, agreement of branch formulas on pairwise model intersections inside \(\mathcal P(\Omega_{\mathcal A})\) does not by itself produce one globally regular rational expression, so semantic gluing is not an admissible completion argument.
honest_scope: The bounded uniform fixing normal form, its lag-switch-hedge grammar, the explicit general state bound \(B_\star(n,L,\gamma)\), and arithmetic compilation on every positive common-law intersection are open. The independent-shift lift, acyclic-summary reduction, explicit lag-switch collision, generic front-door-family inclusion, Assaad-criterion embedding, and the five-state outside-family trace are supplied as to-prove statements, not presumed facts. Passing the front-door, outside-family trace, offset-sensitive fixing, and lag-switch tests for \(|V|\le3\) and \(L=1\) is necessary but not a completeness proof. The statistical theorem is conditional on a successful finite-cylinder output, geometric beta mixing, the Newey--West modified-Bartlett weights, \(h_T\to\infty\), and \(h_T=o(T^{1/4})\); it does not rescue an unidentified query. The finite family \(\mathcal A\) is fixed before the model class is formed and may be nonbinary; every compared model and returned functional lives on the same \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\). Ranking across anomalous regimes would require separate stability assumptions not made here. When \(L=0\), the proposal reduces to ordinary fixed-ADMG ID.

literature_map: The present claim fixes \(\mathcal A\) before forming \(\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)\), so all model comparisons and returned functionals share \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\). The audited comparison map separates results by model, intervention target, graph input, and output certificate. Under causal sufficiency, Assaad, Devijver, Gaussier, Gössler, and Meynaoui (2024), Assumption 1, Definition 4, equation (1), and Theorem 2, study singleton lagged total effects from ESCGs and SCGs and return adjustment sets; the PMLR abstract describes necessary-and-sufficient SCG conditions, while the proceedings theorem is phrased as sufficient. Ferreira and Assaad (2024) completely characterize linear direct effects under no hidden confounding and return two finite adjustment sets. Yvernes, Devijver, and Gaussier (2025) give necessary-and-sufficient common-adjustment conditions, again under causal sufficiency. Under latent confounding, Assaad (2025), Lemmas 4.1--4.5 and Theorem 1, gives a sufficient common front-door functional for selected micro total effects; the explicit family \(\mathfrak F_{\mathrm{FD}}\) abstracts its path-interception and back-door separations, and the frontier theorem proves memberwise TID-SCG success plus a traced identified query outside that family. Ferreira and Assaad (2025) prove do-calculus completeness for macro interventions on whole SCG clusters. Neither supplies general micro-effect completeness. For known fine graphs, Shpitser and Pearl (2008), Sections 3--4 and Appendix A, give recursive ID and hedge completeness for one finite ADMG; Richardson, Robins, Evans, and Shpitser (2023), Sections 2--4, formalize fixing kernels and intrinsic sets in a fixed ADMG; and Jahn, Karnik, and Schulman (2025), Theorem 1.1 and Algorithm 2, localize ordinary ID to a bounded segment of one fully specified periodic latent-confounded graph. For a fixed finite uncertainty representation, Jaber, Ribeiro, Zhang, and Bareinboim (2022) give sound-and-complete conditional-effect identification over the Markov-equivalence class encoded by a PAG. None of those fixed-input results treats a translation-invariant exact-summary class with changing temporal vertices and cross-refinement functional disagreement. Yvernes and coauthors (2025) separate graphwise identification, common proof, and common-functional criteria. Bhattacharya, Nabi, and Shpitser (2022) compile fixed-graph identifying functionals into estimators under independent sampling. Viviano and Bradic (2023) establish beta-mixing inference for a different time-series target. Newey and West (1987), equation (5) and Theorems 1--2 on pp. 704--706, establish the modified Bartlett HAC form, positive-semidefiniteness, and consistency under \(h_T/T^{1/4}\to0\). Duarte and coauthors (2024) reduce fixed discrete causal bounds to polynomial programs, which is excluded as the graph-native mechanism. EasyRCA (Assaad, Ez-zejjari, and Zan, 2023) compares adjustment-based direct effects under independent noises and supplies the applied ranking consumer.

novelty_justification: The exact gap is uniform micro-effect identification over \(\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)\), with \(\mathcal A\) fixed so its members share \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\) while differing in temporal vertices, ancestral margins, intrinsic districts, and instantaneous orders. Causally sufficient SCG total-effect adjustment is already addressed by Assaad, Devijver, Gaussier, Gössler, and Meynaoui, and causally sufficient linear direct-effect completeness by Ferreira--Assaad; neither model contains hidden common causes or requires district fixing.
